outcome_statement: On every counted deal in the window, the node came through on the terms it accepted: it paid as agreed when it bought, and it served as agreed, with the model it named, when it provided.
resolution_rule: a deal is resolved only when every term that applies to it is met
counterparty_note: The peer's book of the same exchange is not held on this node. It is shown as not_available, never as a failure or as agreement.

clauses.check_question: Did the node come through on the terms it accepted?
clauses.label: Paid as agreed
clauses.claim: When the node bought, every invoice it saw has a settlement its own wallet reported, for the invoice's amount.

clauses.check_question: Did the node come through on the terms it accepted?
clauses.label: Served as agreed
clauses.claim: When the node provided, it served the exchange it accepted terms for, and every invoice it issued has a settlement its wallet reported, for the invoice's amount.

clauses.check_question: Did the node come through on the terms it accepted?
clauses.label: Served the model it named
clauses.claim: When the node provided, the model that answered is the model it named. A deal a referee already adjudicated is not judged again: the row carries the sealed verdict, read for this node as the node's own verdict counts read it (corroborated, or contradicted naming the other half, is met; contradicted naming this node is not_met; anything else is not_evaluable). Otherwise the row reads "provider states": the node's own records of the model requested and the model that answered, which no verifier can check against the accepted terms, since those carry the model only inside their digest.
